RAIUC-01.name: Verify AI Is Necessary
RAIUC-01.description: Before committing to an AI/ML approach, verify that AI is required. Traditional software approaches or manual processes must be evaluated as alternatives.
verification_criteria: Requirements document includes a statement confirming why AI/ML is necessary
At least one non-AI alternative was considered and documented with rationale for rejection
If a feature can be solved with deterministic rules, AI must not be used without documented justification

what_to_look_for: Search for any design documents, ADRs, or README sections discussing why AI/ML was chosen
Look for comments in code explaining the rationale for using a model vs. deterministic logic
Check if non-AI alternatives were documented anywhere
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Documentation exists showing AI was chosen deliberately with alternatives considered
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No documentation found — AI appears to have been adopted without justification
audit_guidance.remediation: Write a brief AI use case justification document

RAIUC-02.name: Identify All Stakeholders Including Affected Groups
RAIUC-02.description: Identify not only direct users but also groups who are indirectly affected by AI decisions, including demographic groups who may experience differential outcomes.
verification_criteria: Requirements document identifies all stakeholder categories: direct users, contributing stakeholders, and affected groups
For any AI-driven recommendation or ranking feature, requirements explicitly name which demographic or user groups could be differentially affected
Stakeholder list is referenced in user stories and design artifacts

what_to_look_for: Search requirements docs, user stories, or product specs for stakeholder lists
Look for any mention of demographic groups, affected populations, or indirect users
Check if the system impact on different user groups was ever analyzed
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Stakeholder analysis exists including groups who may be indirectly affected
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: Only direct users mentioned with no analysis of differential impact
audit_guidance.remediation: Add stakeholder analysis to requirements documentation

RAIUC-03.name: Identify the Type of AI Required
RAIUC-03.description: For each AI-powered feature, explicitly identify and justify the type of AI being used: traditional ML, generative AI, or agentic AI.
verification_criteria: Each AI feature is classified as traditional ML, generative AI, or agentic AI
The classification is justified with reference to use case requirements
Higher-risk AI types require proportionally more rigorous design and evaluation documentation
Misaligned choices are flagged as a finding

what_to_look_for: Search for model type declarations, imports, or SDK usage (e.g., bedrock, openai, sklearn, transformers)
Identify whether the system uses: traditional ML, generative AI (LLM), or agentic AI (tool use, multi-step)
Check if the AI type choice is documented and justified
audit_guidance.compliant_if: AI type is clearly identifiable from code AND documented with justification
audit_guidance.partial_if: AI type is identifiable from code but not documented
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: AI type is unclear or misclassified
audit_guidance.remediation: Document AI type and justification in architecture docs

RAIUC-04.name: Map User Journey for AI Interaction Requirements
RAIUC-04.description: Map the full user journey across pre-interaction, interaction, and post-interaction phases. Transparency and human oversight requirements must be identified at each phase.
verification_criteria: Application design includes a user journey map for each AI-powered feature covering all three phases
Transparency requirements are documented
Human override capability is designed into every AI-driven decision flow
Accessibility considerations are documented for AI interaction points

what_to_look_for: Search UI code for AI disclosure messages, loading indicators, or powered by AI labels
Look for pre-interaction onboarding or capability disclosure
Check if users can provide feedback or override AI outputs
Search for post-interaction explanation or reasoning display
audit_guidance.compliant_if: All three phases (pre/during/post) have documented AI interaction requirements
audit_guidance.partial_if: Some phases addressed but not all
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No AI-specific user journey considerations found
audit_guidance.remediation: Map AI interaction requirements and implement missing phases

RAIUC-05.name: Obtain Organizational Approval for AI Use Case
RAIUC-05.description: Identify the regulatory and organizational approval requirements for the AI use case, including applicable regulations and the approval pathway.
verification_criteria: Requirements document identifies the geographic scope and applicable regulatory requirements
Organizational approval process is identified
If regulatory classification is unclear, this is flagged as a risk

what_to_look_for: Search for compliance documentation, legal review records, or approval emails referenced in code comments
Look for regulatory classification (HIPAA, GDPR, FDA, etc.) in any documentation
Check if the AI feature went through any formal review process
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Evidence of regulatory scope identification and approval pathway
audit_guidance.unknown_if: No documentation found — requires human confirmation
audit_guidance.remediation: Document regulatory requirements and approval pathway

RAIUC-06.name: Define AI Inputs, Outputs, and Input Variation
RAIUC-06.description: Document what goes into the AI system, what comes out, and how inputs could systematically vary. Distinguish intrinsic variations (system should attend to) from confounding variations (system should ignore). This drives robustness design decisions.
verification_criteria: Requirements or design document specifies AI system inputs at a high level
Expected outputs are described including type and format
Intrinsic input variations are identified (differences the system must handle)
Confounding input variations are identified (differences the system should ignore)
Edge cases and out-of-distribution scenarios are documented

what_to_look_for: Search for input validation schemas, request models, or API contracts defining what the AI accepts
Look for output schemas or response models defining what the AI returns
Search for robustness tests or edge case tests covering input variation
Check if documentation describes what types of inputs the system handles vs. rejects
Look for input sanitization or normalization logic that handles variation
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Input/output types documented AND input variation scenarios identified with handling strategy
audit_guidance.partial_if: Input/output types documented but no variation analysis
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No documentation of what the AI system accepts or produces
audit_guidance.remediation: Document AI input/output specification and identify intrinsic vs confounding input variations

RAIDD-01.name: Fairness Assessment in Design
RAIDD-01.description: Every AI feature that produces recommendations, rankings, or decisions affecting users must include a fairness assessment. The assessment must identify potential sources of bias and define fairness metrics.
verification_criteria: Functional design includes a Fairness Assessment section for each AI-powered component
Potential bias sources are identified: training data bias, feature selection bias, feedback loop bias, proxy discrimination
Fairness metrics are defined appropriate to the use case
Mitigation strategies for identified bias sources are documented

what_to_look_for: Search for diversity injection, result shuffling, or demographic balancing in recommendation/ranking code
Look for fairness metrics, bias tests, or demographic parity checks in test files
Search for any bias mitigation patterns (e.g., re-ranking, minimum diversity requirements)
Check if training data documentation mentions demographic representation
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Fairness assessment documented AND at least one mitigation strategy implemented
audit_guidance.partial_if: Fairness mentioned in docs but no implementation evidence, OR implementation exists but undocumented
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No fairness consideration found in code or documentation
audit_guidance.remediation: Conduct fairness assessment and implement diversity injection

RAIDD-02.name: Explainability by Design
RAIDD-02.description: Every AI feature that produces a recommendation or decision visible to a user must be designed with explainability as a first-class requirement. The level of explainability must be proportional to the impact of the decision.
verification_criteria: Functional design specifies what explanation will be shown to the user for each AI output
The explanation mechanism is designed into the data model and API — not added as a post-hoc label
For high-impact decisions, the explanation must reference the actual factors used
Explainability requirements are included in the API design and UI specifications

what_to_look_for: Search API response schemas for explanation fields, reason codes, or factor arrays
Look for UI components that display why information alongside AI outputs
Search for explanation, reason, factors, match_factors, confidence fields in response objects
Check if explanations reference actual model inputs vs. generic messages
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Structured explanation data returned with every AI output AND displayed to users
audit_guidance.partial_if: Some explanation exists but it is generic rather than factor-based
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No explanation mechanism found — AI outputs are opaque to users
audit_guidance.remediation: Add explanation fields to AI response API and surface them in UI

RAIDD-03.name: Privacy by Design for AI Features
RAIDD-03.description: AI features that use personal or sensitive data as input signals must apply privacy-by-design principles. Data minimization, purpose limitation, and consent must be addressed in the design.
verification_criteria: Functional design identifies exactly which personal or sensitive data fields are used as inputs to AI features
Data minimization is applied: only the minimum data necessary for the AI feature is used
Purpose limitation is documented
The design specifies whether personal data is used for model training and what consent mechanism applies
Differential privacy or anonymization techniques are evaluated and documented

what_to_look_for: Search for conversation/session storage — are user inputs persisted beyond the session?
Look for personal or sensitive data fields being passed to AI models (names, health data, financial data, demographics)
Check logging configuration — are user inputs or model prompts logged in plain text?
Search for data minimization patterns (only necessary fields sent to model)
audit_guidance.compliant_if: User inputs not persisted beyond session, personal data minimized, logs redacted
audit_guidance.partial_if: Some privacy controls exist but gaps remain (e.g., inputs logged in plain text)
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: User inputs persisted without consent, personal data sent to model unnecessarily, or inputs logged
audit_guidance.remediation: Implement session-only storage, PII/sensitive data redaction in logs, data minimization

RAIDD-04.name: Safety and Harm Prevention Design
RAIDD-04.description: The design must explicitly identify potential harms from AI outputs and include safeguards to prevent or mitigate them. This includes both direct harms and indirect harms.
verification_criteria: Functional design includes a Potential Harms section for each AI feature
Both direct and indirect harm scenarios are documented
Safeguards are designed for each identified harm
The design specifies what happens when the AI cannot produce a confident output (graceful degradation)
The design must not allow the AI to operate outside its documented scope

what_to_look_for: Search for content filtering, input validation, or safety checks BEFORE the AI model is called
Look for denied topics, blocked patterns, or safety classifiers
Search for graceful degradation — what happens when the AI cannot produce a safe output?
For high-risk domains (healthcare, finance, legal): search for domain-specific safety guardrails
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Pre-model safety gate exists AND graceful degradation is implemented
audit_guidance.partial_if: Post-model filtering exists but no pre-model gate, OR safety exists but no graceful degradation
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No safety filtering found — all user input reaches the model unfiltered
audit_guidance.remediation: Add pre-model content gate and graceful degradation fallback

RAIDD-05.name: Human Oversight and Controllability
RAIDD-05.description: Every AI feature must be designed with explicit human oversight mechanisms. Humans must be able to monitor, adjust, override, and if necessary shut down AI features without requiring code changes.
verification_criteria: Application design includes an admin/ops capability to monitor AI output quality metrics
Override mechanisms exist at multiple levels: end user, admin, engineering
Feature flags or kill switches for AI features are included in the infrastructure design
Audit logging captures AI inputs, outputs, and any human overrides
The design specifies who has authority to override AI decisions and under what circumstances

what_to_look_for: Search for feature flags, environment variables, or config settings that disable AI features
Look for escalation paths — can users request human assistance?
Search for admin monitoring dashboards or quality metric tracking
Check if AI can be disabled without a code deployment (kill switch pattern)
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Kill switch exists + user escalation path + admin monitoring capability
audit_guidance.partial_if: Some oversight mechanisms exist but not all three
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No way to disable AI without code change, no escalation path, no monitoring
audit_guidance.remediation: Add kill switch env var, escalation UI, and monitoring metrics

RAIDD-06.name: Data Governance for AI Training and Inference
RAIDD-06.description: The design must document the data governance model for all data used in AI features — both at inference time and if applicable at training time.
verification_criteria: NFR requirements include data lineage documentation for AI input data
The source, quality, and known limitations of data used for AI features are documented
Data retention policies for AI inference logs are defined
The design specifies how data quality issues are handled at inference time

what_to_look_for: Search for model version pinning (hardcoded model IDs vs. latest)
Look for data lineage documentation — what data feeds the AI?
Check if inference input/output is logged with appropriate retention policies
Search for model registry or versioning artifacts
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Model version pinned, data lineage documented, inference logging configured
audit_guidance.partial_if: Model version pinned but no data lineage, OR logging exists but no retention policy
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: Model version unpinned (latest), no data lineage, no inference logging
audit_guidance.remediation: Pin model version, document data lineage, configure inference logging

RAIDD-07.name: Identify Veracity, Robustness, and Security Harms
RAIDD-07.description: Explicitly identify hallucination risks, robustness failure modes (input variation causing wrong outputs), and adversarial/security risks (prompt injection, jailbreaking). Each must have a documented mitigation strategy.
verification_criteria: Functional design identifies hallucination and veracity risks with mitigations
Robustness failure modes from input variation are documented
Adversarial input risks (prompt injection, jailbreaking) are identified
Security protections are designed into the core AI system
Output filtering for hallucinations is specified
Design choices that introduced new risks are documented

what_to_look_for: Search for hallucination detection, grounding checks, or factual accuracy validation
Look for prompt injection detection or jailbreak prevention patterns
Search for input sanitization that handles adversarial inputs
Check for robustness tests covering unexpected or malformed inputs
Look for output validation that checks factual consistency
Search for security-specific guardrails or content filters
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Hallucination mitigation documented AND adversarial input protection implemented AND robustness tests exist
audit_guidance.partial_if: Some protections exist but not all three categories addressed
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No hallucination mitigation, no adversarial protection, and no robustness testing
audit_guidance.remediation: Add hallucination detection, prompt injection protection, and robustness test cases

RAIER-01.name: Pre-Release RAI Review Planning
RAIER-01.description: The code generation plan for any unit containing AI/ML features must include explicit test steps for the pre-release RAI review. RAI evaluation must be a named, checkboxed step in the generation plan.
verification_criteria: Code generation plan includes all applicable RAI review test steps as named checkboxes
RAI test steps are not grouped under a generic testing step — they are explicitly named
Each RAI test step references the corresponding RAIDD design rule it validates

what_to_look_for: Search CI/CD pipeline configs for RAI-specific test steps
Look for test files with fairness, bias, or safety test cases
Check if code generation or release checklists include RAI review items
audit_guidance.compliant_if: RAI test steps exist in CI/CD AND test files cover fairness/safety/explainability
audit_guidance.partial_if: Some RAI tests exist but not systematically included in release process
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No RAI-specific tests found in test suite or CI/CD pipeline
audit_guidance.remediation: Add RAI test steps to CI/CD and create RAI test file

RAIER-02.name: Pre-Release Stakeholder Review and Go/No-Go Decision
RAIER-02.description: Before any AI feature is considered ready for deployment, the build and test instructions must include a structured stakeholder review step with a documented go/no-go decision.
verification_criteria: Build and test instructions include a RAI Pre-Release Review section
The review checklist covers: fairness, bias, privacy, safety, explainability test results
Stakeholder roles for the review are identified
A rai-release-review.md artifact is included in the build and test output files
No-go criteria are explicitly stated

what_to_look_for: Search for release checklists, deployment runbooks, or approval workflows
Look for any documented go/no-go criteria for AI features
Check if responsible AI review is part of the release process
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Formal RAI review process with named approvers documented
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No release review process found, or AI features deploy without any RAI gate
audit_guidance.unknown_if: Release process exists but RAI review not explicitly included
audit_guidance.remediation: Create RAI pre-release review checklist and integrate into release process

RAIER-03.name: Fairness and Bias Test Coverage
RAIER-03.description: The test suite for any AI unit must include tests that specifically evaluate fairness and bias using representative test data that covers the demographic and contextual diversity of the expected user population.
verification_criteria: Unit test instructions include fairness test cases with representative test data
Test data covers diverse user profiles
Tests verify that AI output quality does not systematically differ across user demographic groups
Bias test results are documented with quantitative metrics where applicable

what_to_look_for: Search test files for demographic diversity in test data
Look for tests that verify AI output quality across different user groups
Check if bias amplification is tested
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Test suite includes diverse test data AND tests verify parity across groups
audit_guidance.partial_if: Some diversity in test data but no explicit parity verification
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: Test data is homogeneous or no fairness-specific tests exist
audit_guidance.remediation: Add diverse test data and fairness parity test cases

RAIER-04.name: Model and System Traceability
RAIER-04.description: Every AI component must have documented traceability: what data was used, what model or algorithm was applied, what version is deployed, and what evaluation results were recorded.
verification_criteria: Build and test instructions include a step to record AI component metadata
The rai-release-review.md artifact includes a traceability section
If a pre-trained model is used, its version is pinned and documented
Evaluation results are recorded alongside the traceability metadata

what_to_look_for: Search for model version documentation (README, config files, deployment manifests)
Look for training data documentation or data cards
Check if evaluation results are recorded anywhere
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Model version, training data description, and evaluation results all documented
audit_guidance.partial_if: Model version documented but training data or evaluation results missing
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No model documentation found — cannot determine what model is running or why
audit_guidance.remediation: Create model card / system card documenting model, data, and evaluation

RAIER-05.name: Graceful Degradation and Fallback Validation
RAIER-05.description: The test suite must include tests that validate graceful degradation behavior — what happens when the AI cannot produce a confident or safe recommendation. The fallback must be tested explicitly.
verification_criteria: Test cases cover: no matching results found, AI confidence below threshold, AI service unavailable, malformed input data
Each scenario has a documented expected fallback behavior
Fallback behavior does not expose AI internals or error details to the user
Tests verify that fallback paths do not bypass access control or data privacy requirements

what_to_look_for: Search for try/catch blocks around AI calls with meaningful fallback behavior
Look for timeout handling, circuit breakers, or fallback responses
Check if fallback paths are tested
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Graceful degradation implemented AND tested for key failure scenarios
audit_guidance.partial_if: Some error handling exists but fallback behavior is generic (500 error) or untested
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: AI failures propagate as unhandled errors to users
audit_guidance.remediation: Implement and test graceful degradation for AI service unavailability

RAIOP-01.name: AI Performance and Fairness Monitoring
RAIOP-01.description: The build and test instructions must include operational readiness steps for monitoring AI feature performance and fairness in production. Monitoring must be designed before deployment.
verification_criteria: Build and test instructions include an Operational Readiness — AI Monitoring section
Monitoring requirements are specified for each AI feature: what metrics, what thresholds, what alerting
Fairness drift monitoring is explicitly included
Infrastructure design includes the monitoring infrastructure

what_to_look_for: Search for custom metrics, dashboards, or alerting configs related to AI features
Look for recommendation quality metrics, override rates, or user satisfaction tracking
Check if fairness drift monitoring exists (tracking demographic distribution over time)
audit_guidance.compliant_if: AI-specific metrics defined + fairness drift monitoring + alerting configured
audit_guidance.partial_if: Basic performance metrics exist but no fairness monitoring
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No AI-specific monitoring — only generic infrastructure metrics
audit_guidance.remediation: Add AI quality metrics and fairness drift monitoring

RAIOP-02.name: AI Incident Response Plan
RAIOP-02.description: The build and test summary must include an AI-specific incident response plan. AI incidents are distinct from standard software incidents — they may involve subtle, systematic harms.
verification_criteria: Build and test summary includes an AI Incident Response section covering detection, classification, containment, investigation, recovery, communication
Feature flag / kill switch for AI features is confirmed as implemented
Escalation path for AI incidents is defined
Applicable regulatory notification requirements are addressed

what_to_look_for: Search runbooks, incident response docs, or on-call guides for AI-specific procedures
Look for severity classification that includes AI-specific incidents (bias, harmful output)
Check if there is a documented process for disabling AI features in an incident
audit_guidance.compliant_if: AI incident response plan exists with severity levels and kill switch procedure
audit_guidance.partial_if: Requirements or design documents specify incident response intent (kill switch, monitoring, escalation) but no dedicated runbook or operational artifact exists yet
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No incident response documentation, kill switch, or escalation path found anywhere
audit_guidance.unknown_if: No documentation provided and no code evidence of any incident handling
audit_guidance.remediation: Create AI incident response runbook

RAIOP-03.name: Ongoing Governance and Review Cadence
RAIOP-03.description: The build and test instructions must specify a governance review cadence for AI features post-deployment. AI systems must not be deployed and forgotten.
verification_criteria: Build and test summary includes a Post-Deployment AI Governance section
Review cadence is specified with concrete timeframes
Retirement criteria are documented
Governance review outputs are linked to the system registry

what_to_look_for: Search for scheduled reviews, recurring calendar items, or governance documentation
Look for model refresh schedules or retraining triggers
Check if there is a documented process for retiring or replacing AI features
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Governance cadence documented with concrete timeframes and retirement criteria
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No governance cadence found — AI features deployed and forgotten
audit_guidance.unknown_if: Reviews may happen informally but not documented
audit_guidance.remediation: Document governance review schedule and retirement criteria

RAIOP-04.name: User Feedback Loop
RAIOP-04.description: AI features must have a mechanism for users to provide feedback on AI outputs in production. This feedback must be collected, monitored, and acted upon.
verification_criteria: Code generation includes a user feedback mechanism for AI-powered features
Feedback data is stored and accessible for analysis
Build and test instructions include a step to verify the feedback collection mechanism works
Operational readiness section specifies how feedback is reviewed and what threshold triggers investigation

what_to_look_for: Search UI code for thumbs up/down, rating widgets, or report a problem features on AI outputs
Look for feedback storage and analysis pipelines
Check if negative feedback triggers any investigation or alerting
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Feedback mechanism in UI + feedback stored + threshold triggers investigation
audit_guidance.partial_if: Feedback UI exists but data not analyzed or no threshold alerting
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No user feedback mechanism on AI outputs
audit_guidance.remediation: Add feedback widget to AI output UI and feedback analysis pipeline

RAIOP-05.name: Transparency to Users About AI Use
RAIOP-05.description: Users must be clearly informed that AI is being used to generate recommendations or make decisions that affect them. This transparency must be implemented in the product.
verification_criteria: UI/UX design and code generation include visible disclosure that AI is being used
The disclosure is present at the point of AI interaction
Users can access a plain-language explanation of how the AI works and what data it uses
Build and test instructions include a test case verifying that AI disclosure is present and accurate

what_to_look_for: Search UI code for AI, powered by, automated, or similar disclosure labels near AI outputs
Look for privacy policy or terms of service mentioning AI use
Check if users can access an explanation of how the AI works
audit_guidance.compliant_if: Visible AI disclosure at point of interaction + accessible explanation of AI use
audit_guidance.partial_if: Disclosure exists in privacy policy/ToS but not at point of interaction
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No disclosure found — users cannot tell they are interacting with AI
audit_guidance.remediation: Add AI disclosure label at point of interaction

RAIOP-06.name: System Card and User Guidance Documentation
RAIOP-06.description: A system card documenting intended use, limitations, and failure modes must be created. A plan for keeping it current must exist. Guidance for users on how to responsibly adjust system behavior must be provided.
verification_criteria: A system card exists documenting intended use cases and limitations
Failure modes and their handling are documented in the system card
A plan for publishing and updating the system card is defined
User guidance on how to responsibly change system behavior is provided

what_to_look_for: Search for a system card, model card, or AI service card document
Look for documentation of intended use cases and explicitly out-of-scope uses
Check if failure modes and limitations are documented for users
Search for user guidance on adjusting AI system behavior
audit_guidance.compliant_if: System card exists with intended use, limitations, failure modes, AND user guidance on behavior adjustment
audit_guidance.partial_if: Some documentation exists but system card is incomplete or missing user guidance
audit_guidance.non_compliant_if: No system card or equivalent documentation found
audit_guidance.remediation: Create system card documenting intended use, limitations, failure modes, and user guidance
